decision.explanation: Initial priorities were the reference-separating full-band PSD/estimator shape, harmonic families, carrier-band envelopes, and impulsiveness maps; time-frequency, persistence, cepstrum and cyclic views were then used as correlated controls rather than independent votes. The best-supported match is C06 (bowed_rotor): R06 is nearest in the declared full-band Welch baseline and harmonic-spacing control, has the closest cyclic signature, and shares the query's detailed approximately 29.9 Hz-related frequency family [Q01.C01.S0001, D03.harmonics, D03.cyclic, R06.C01.S0001, R06.harmonics, R06.cyclic]. Strong counterevidence is the different dominant line (query 89.6 Hz versus R06 44.9 Hz), different carrier-band modulation, absence of R06's level changes, and much lower query filter-bank kurtosis [D03.envelope_1, D03.envelope_4, D03.kurtosis_bank, R06.envelope_1, R06.envelope_4, R06.kurtosis_bank]. Other controls conflict: estimator/STFT views favor R04, cepstrum and persistence favor R03, modulation map favors R05, and kurtosis favors low-impulsiveness references. Thus the decision is driven mainly by numeric baseline plus detailed harmonic-family alignment, not image proximity alone. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for query and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied [D03.orders, D03.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. The result supports condition-level similarity to C06 with material acquisition/regime ambiguity; it does not independently prove fault mechanism, component, or severity.
